title: Prophecy and Fulfillment
description: Old Testament promises paired with their New Testament fulfillments, read in sequence: promise first, then the passage that claims it fulfilled.
audience: A reader who wants to see the Bible's promise-and-fulfillment architecture with their own eyes.

sequence.note: The first promise: the woman's seed will crush the serpent.
The second Adam undoes the first (ch. 5) — and at the letter's close, 'the God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet' (16:20).
All nations blessed through Abraham's seed.
Paul: 'the seed is Christ' — and the nations are being blessed.
A prophet like Moses will arise (ch. 18).
Pentecost first: the Spirit falls and Peter preaches the risen Christ. Everything the apostles say next stands on this.
Peter names Jesus as that prophet.
A son of David on an everlasting throne.
Gabriel to Mary: 'the throne of his father David… his kingdom will never end.'
Immanuel; a child called Mighty God.
And the ruler will come from little Bethlehem.
Matthew quotes both: virgin and Immanuel, Bethlehem and the shepherd-king.
A messenger will prepare the way; Elijah will come first.
John the Baptist — camel hair, wilderness, 'prepare the way.'
The Spirit-anointed herald of good news to the poor (ch. 61).
'Today this scripture is fulfilled in your hearing.'
Forsaken, mocked, pierced, garments divided.
The Servant crushed for our iniquities.
The passion narratives quote and echo both throughout.
'By his wounds you have been healed' — Isaiah 53 preached to the church.
David's Lord at God's right hand, a priest forever.
Hebrews builds the whole priesthood of Christ on that psalm.
A new covenant: law on hearts, sins remembered no more.
Quoted in full and declared in force through Christ's one offering.
'I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh.'
A new heart, and my Spirit within you.
One like a son of man receives everlasting dominion.
John sees him — 'coming with the clouds; every eye will see him.'
The pierced one; the fountain opened for sin.
'They will look on him whom they have pierced' — cited at the cross.
The river of life from the sanctuary; the LORD is there.
Every thread ties off: new creation, God with us, the tree of life open again.
